Podcaster • Moderator • Storyteller • Community Builder

I turn lived experience into stories, dialogue and action.

My work sits where media, public dialogue and social impact meet. I create conversations that make complex ideas human, preserve stories that deserve to be remembered, and build projects that bring people together across borders. From podcast studios in Norway to dialogue rooms with Syrians and a 5,000-kilometre journey from Oslo to Damascus, I use storytelling as a way to connect people, ideas and possibilities.

From Damascus to Oslo — and back by bicycle. One of those stories became a 5,000-kilometre bicycle journey from Oslo to Damascus — a public media and fundraising initiative created to support education in Syria and bring people into the story along the way.

Podcasts

Two podcast formats, one purpose: creating space for ideas and experiences that are often separated by language, geography and public debate. I develop the concepts, prepare and host the conversations, and help shape each episode from research to publication.

17 episodes
HostProducerEditor

غربيين (Gharbiyyin)

غربيين brings Western researchers and specialists working on the Middle East into Arabic-language conversations. I translate academic and expert knowledge into accessible, thoughtful dialogue — giving Arabic-speaking audiences direct access to the people behind the research and the ideas shaping how the region is understood.

  • Purpose: bridge research communities and Arabic-speaking audiences.
  • Approach: research-led preparation, structured interviews and accessible conversation.
  • Impact: knowledge exchange, nuance and stronger public understanding across cultures.

رحلة (Rehla)

رحلة is an oral-history podcast about Syrians whose lives were reshaped by war, displacement and starting again. Through long-form, personal conversations, guests tell their stories in their own words — not only what happened to them, but what they built, learned and became along the way.

  • Purpose: preserve Syrian stories in the voices of the people who lived them.
  • Approach: intimate, story-led conversations built around one person and one journey.
  • Impact: a growing human archive of memory, identity, resilience and belonging.

Syrian Dialogue

After the fall of the Assad regime, I wanted to create a space where Syrians could practise something that decades of authoritarian rule had made difficult: disagreeing openly, listening seriously and imagining the country’s future together.

Published in Internasjonal Politikk

The Syrian Dialogue — creating space for a different political culture

I initiated and facilitated a series of Syrian dialogue meetings in Oslo and Trondheim, bringing together Syrians across political, ethnic, religious and social backgrounds. Meeting roughly every two weeks, participants explored identity, justice, democracy, reconciliation and the institutions Syria might need next. I later documented the initiative and its lessons in an article published by Internasjonal Politikk.

“Structured dialogue can help build trust, create space for disagreement, and lay the groundwork for democratic culture.”
  • Format: recurring dialogue meetings in Oslo and Trondheim, approximately every two weeks.
  • Themes: identity, justice, democracy, reconciliation, institutions and Syria’s future.
  • My role: initiator, facilitator and writer — designing a space where disagreement could become constructive rather than divisive.

Cycling4Hope

A 5,000-kilometre return journey became my largest public storytelling project: a 66-day bicycle campaign from Oslo to Damascus that connected a personal story of migration and return with a concrete mission to support education in Syria.

5,000 km
FundraisingMedia coveragePartnerships

Cycling4Hope — 5,000 km from Oslo to Damascus

Over 66 days, I cycled from Norway to Syria, documenting the journey and using it to mobilize attention and support for education. The campaign raised approximately USD 13,000, was developed with partners including Molham Team and Oslo Sykkelverksted, and attracted coverage from major Arabic and international media. It combined endurance, fundraising, partnership-building and real-time storytelling into one public campaign.

  • Mission: turn a personal return journey into tangible support for education in Syria.
  • Reach: extensive journey documentation, partnerships and coverage across major media outlets.
  • What it demonstrates: initiative, resilience, campaign execution, partnership-building and the ability to carry a story across borders.

On the road

Journey

Thousands of kilometres across Europe and toward Syria turned the road itself into a storytelling platform — each stage adding people, conversations and momentum to the campaign.

Resilience

Reality of the trip

The project was built in real time: long days on the bicycle, changing weather, camping, logistics and uncertainty. The physical challenge was part of the message — commitment made visible.

Community leadership

Long before my media projects, community work taught me how to build trust, organize people and turn an idea into something others want to be part of. That experience remains central to how I lead projects and communicate today.

Syrian Student Association

I co-founded the Syrian Student Association in Norway in 2019 and helped grow it into a platform supporting Arabic-speaking students as they navigated education and student life. I led volunteer teams, developed activities and partnerships, and helped create a community where students could find practical guidance, networks and a sense of belonging.

  • Community events and ceremonies reaching 200–300 participants.
  • Guidance for students entering Norwegian schools and universities and navigating study life.
  • Leadership of volunteer teams of roughly 5–12 people, with responsibility for coordination, communication and delivery.

I bring the perspective of a technologist and consultant, the instincts of a storyteller, and years of experience building communities and projects from the ground up. If you are building something that needs trust, curiosity, initiative and the ability to connect different worlds, I would be glad to talk.
